Group characteristics are shown in Table 1, and the type of surgery for the patient groups is shown in Supplementary Table 1. Cancer was the underlying condition in 73% of group 1 patients and 85% of patients in the usual care group. The overall transfusion rate in the study was 20.8%. Ten patients in the usual care group (10/32 = 31.25%) were transfused vs 5 in the intervention group (5/40 = 12.5%), equating to a 60% relative reduction in transfusions between the 2 groups shown in Table 2. section_outputs_json: {"introduction": {"selected_paragraphs_json": "[{\"pnum\": 4, \"paragraph_text\": \"Introduction\", \"sentences\": [{\"sid\": \"S12\", \"text\": \"Introduction\"}]}, {\"pnum\": 5, \"paragraph_text\": \"Obesity is a growing problem in industrialized countries, where approximately one-third of the population is obese, and has been associated with a number of health problems, including diabetes, heart disease, different types of cancer, and decreased life expectancy (1). Knockout mice for the 5-HT2c receptors have a higher body weight as a result of abnormal food consumption, further confirming the role of this receptor in obesity (4). section_outputs_json: {"introduction": {"selected_paragraphs_json": "[{\"pnum\": 13, \"paragraph_text\": \"Introduction\", \"sentences\": [{\"sid\": \"S24\", \"text\": \"Introduction\"}]}, {\"pnum\": 14, \"paragraph_text\": \"Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease that leads to morbidity resulting in high societal costs.1 2 While disease modifying antirheumatic drugs such as methotrexate (MTX) have significantly improved the outcome in RA, not all patients respond.3 The advent of biological agents including tumour necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitors has revolutionised the treatment of RA;3 4 however the high cost is a significant burden to the patient and society.5\", \"sentences\": [{\"sid\": \"S25\", \"text\": \"Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease that leads to morbidity resulting in high societal costs.1 2\"}, {\"sid\": \"S26\", \"text\": \"While disease modifying antirheumatic drugs such as methotrexate (MTX) have significantly improved the outcome in RA, not all patients respond.3\"}, {\"sid\": \"S27\", \"text\": \"The advent of biological agents including tumour necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitors has revolutionised the treatment of RA;3 4 however the high cost is a significant burden to the patient and society.5\"}]}, {\"pnum\": 15, \"paragraph_text\": \"A biosimilar is a biologic agent that contains a (similar) version of the active substance of an already authorised original biological medicinal (reference) product.6 Due to the complexity of the manufacturing process, biosimilars differ from generic drugs in the chemical drug area.6 7 Thus, the approval pathway of biosimilars is different from generics; very roughly three major steps are employed.8 First, a comprehensive physicochemical and biological characterisation6 is done to prove similarity on the molecular level (including in vivo and in vitro assays), second, a pharmacokinetic (PK) study is done to show bioequivalence, and finally, an efficacy study (usually a randomised controlled study) is done to demonstrate clinical equivalence, compared with the reference product. The development of Remsima (code name CT-P13, Celltrion, Incheon, Korea), a biosimilar of infliximab (Remicade, Janssen Biotech, Horsham, Pennsylvania, USA), has followed this process9–11 and recently been approved by the European Medicines Agency.12 The development of biosimilars is anticipated to greatly decrease the economic burden of biological therapy.13\", \"sentences\": [{\"sid\": \"S28\", \"text\": \"A biosimilar is a biologic agent that contains a (similar) version of the active substance of an already authorised original biological medicinal (reference) product.6\"}, {\"sid\": \"S29\", \"text\": \"Due to the complexity of the manufacturing process, biosimilars differ from generic drugs in the chemical drug area.6 7\"}, {\"sid\": \"S30\", \"text\": \"Thus, the approval pathway of biosimilars is different from generics; very roughly three major steps are employed.8\"}, {\"sid\": \"S31\", \"text\": \"First, a comprehensive physicochemical and biological characterisation6 is done to prove similarity on the molecular level (including in vivo and in vitro assays), second, a pharmacokinetic (PK) study is done to show bioequivalence, and finally, an efficacy study (usually a randomised controlled study) is done to demonstrate clinical equivalence, compared with the reference product.\"}, {\"sid\": \"S32\", \"text\": \"The development of Remsima (code name CT-P13, Celltrion, Incheon, Korea), a biosimilar of infliximab (Remicade, Janssen Biotech, Horsham, Pennsylvania, USA), has followed this process9–11 and recently been approved by the European Medicines Agency.12\"}, {\"sid\": \"S33\", \"text\": \"The development of biosimilars is anticipated to greatly decrease the economic burden of biological therapy.13\"}]}, {\"pnum\": 16, \"paragraph_text\": \"SB2 is developed as a biosimilar of infliximab. section_outputs_json: {"introduction": {"selected_paragraphs_json": "[{\"pnum\": 11, \"paragraph_text\": \"Introduction\", \"sentences\": [{\"sid\": \"S22\", \"text\": \"Introduction\"}]}, {\"pnum\": 12, \"paragraph_text\": \"Cardiovascular (CV) disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA).1 Conventional risk factors do not account fully for this, and increased levels of inflammation associated with RA may be an important determinant of CV outcomes.2 In a study of 651 patients, an elevated inflammatory state was associated with an increased CV event rate but a paradoxical reduction in circulating lipid levels.3 This suggests that the relationship between lipid levels and increased CV disease is altered in RA and may be explained, at least in part, by qualitative changes to lipoproteins as a result of the inflammatory milieu.\", \"sentences\": [{\"sid\": \"S23\", \"text\": \"Cardiovascular (CV) disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA).1\"}, {\"sid\": \"S24\", \"text\": \"Conventional risk factors do not account fully for this, and increased levels of inflammation associated with RA may be an important determinant of CV outcomes.2\"}, {\"sid\": \"S25\", \"text\": \"In a study of 651 patients, an elevated inflammatory state was associated with an increased CV event rate but a paradoxical reduction in circulating lipid levels.3\"}, {\"sid\": \"S26\", \"text\": \"This suggests that the relationship between lipid levels and increased CV disease is altered in RA and may be explained, at least in part, by qualitative changes to lipoproteins as a result of the inflammatory milieu.\"}]}, {\"pnum\": 13, \"paragraph_text\": \"High-density lipoprotein (HDL) has been suggested to exert anti-atherosclerotic effects via reverse cholesterol transport and activation of protective endothelial pathways. In conditions such as RA however, HDL has been shown to acquire pro-inflammatory and pro-thrombotic phenotype that can promote atherogenesis and potentially increase CV risk.4 5 A previous study from our group demonstrated that the beneficial function of HDL can be restored after resolution of acute inflammatory stimulus, suggesting that the modification of systemic inflammation offers potential for CV risk reduction.6\", \"sentences\": [{\"sid\": \"S27\", \"text\": \"High-density lipoprotein (HDL) has been suggested to exert anti-atherosclerotic effects via reverse cholesterol transport and activation of protective endothelial pathways.\"}, {\"sid\": \"S28\", \"text\": \"In conditions such as RA however, HDL has been shown to acquire pro-inflammatory and pro-thrombotic phenotype that can promote atherogenesis and potentially increase CV risk.4 5\"}, {\"sid\": \"S29\", \"text\": \"A previous study from our group demonstrated that the beneficial function of HDL can be restored after resolution of acute inflammatory stimulus, suggesting that the modification of systemic inflammation offers potential for CV risk reduction.6\"}]}, {\"pnum\": 14, \"paragraph_text\": \"In our current study, we examined the influence of standard (methotrexate (MTX)) and novel anti-inflammatory treatments (infliximab) on HDL function in patients with RA in a randomised controlled trial over 1 year.
